title: Pygmalion Effect in Vision: Image-to-Clay Translation for Reflective Geometry Reconstruction
abstract: arXiv:2511.21098v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Understanding reflection remains a long-standing challenge in 3D reconstruction due to the entanglement of appearance and geometry under view-dependent reflections. In this work, we present the Pygmalion Effect in Vision, a novel framework that metaphorically "sculpts" reflective objects into clay-like forms through image-to-clay translation. We then introduce a dual-branch design in which a BRDF-based reflective branch and a clay-guided branch share the same Gaussian geometry but operate through independent rendering paths. The clay-guided branch, supervised by the synthesized clay images, provides reflection-free geometric guidance that complements the photometric supervision of the BRDF branch. Experiments on both synthetic and real datasets show consistent improvements in both geometry and photometric metrics. translated_title: 视觉中的皮格马利翁效应：面向反射几何重建的图像到粘土转换
translated_abstract: 由于视角相关反射下外观与几何的相互纠缠，理解反射始终是3D重建领域的一项长期挑战。在本工作中，我们提出了“视觉中的皮格马利翁效应”，这是一个新颖的框架，通过图像到粘土的转换，将反射性物体隐喻性地“雕琢”成粘土状形态。我们进一步引入了一种双分支设计：基于BRDF的反射分支与粘土引导分支共享相同的高斯几何，但通过各自独立的渲染路径进行运作。粘土引导分支由合成的粘土图像进行监督，能够提供无反射的几何引导，与BRDF分支的光度监督形成互补。在合成数据集与真实数据集上的实验表明，该方法在几何和光度指标上均取得了一致的提升。除技术层面的收获外，我们的框架还揭示了一种“以无光观形”的理念——通过将辐射度转化为中性状态来实现对物体的观察……
tldr: 该论文提出“视觉中的皮格马利翁效应”框架，通过图像到粘土转换将反射物体“雕琢”为无反射的粘土形态，并采用共享高斯几何的双分支设计（BRDF反射分支与粘土引导分支）实现反射物体的高精度几何重建。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the "Pygmalion Effect in Vision" framework, which metaphorically "sculpts" reflective objects into clay-like forms via image-to-clay translation, employing a dual-branch design with a BRDF-based reflective branch and a clay-guided branch sharing the same Gaussian geometry for accurate reflective geometry reconstruction.
